thaw_reason: Round five returned 15 coverage gaps — agents naming bytes they were not handed — across nine surfaces, and every one of them is a reads: line. Ruled blocking rather than deferred to v0.5.3: the gaps sit on the release's own claims about itself (the site could not read the CHANGELOG it must agree with; release-procedure could not check the surface count it states seven times; the changelog surface could not check the SILENT item every consumer must act on), so deferring them means shipping a release whose central claims went unadjudicated. Thawed once, for all nine surfaces together, rather than seven times. | SECOND THAW, 15 Aug: the priority design adds a machine-readable reach_class to every surface entry — the field the P0-P3 matrix reads. Ruled blocking for the same reason as the first thaw: the change is to the gate's own question, and round seven must run under it. | THIRD THAW, 15 Aug: round seven returned two coverage gaps, both reported by the agents themselves rather than found afterwards. install-scripts said it could not check three of its own claims because scripts/ci/dossierx-check.yml — the file both installers send a consumer to for the AUTHORITY half of the gate — was not in its bundle; that finding is a P1 and blocks regardless. roadmap said the write_conflict entry asserts what the router bundle currently says, while `skills` is one of the fingerprints this release's delta reports as CHANGED. Ruled blocking rather than deferred to v0.5.3 for the reason the first thaw gives: both gaps sit on claims this release makes about itself, and deferring them ships a release whose own installers admit they were judged against a file nobody read. Two reads: lines, no other manifest change.
